bull.b: Improving revenue and exceptional gross margins indicate attractive product economics as PEMGARDA gains traction. If commercial adoption continues and future products launch successfully, these economics could support scalable revenue growth despite current development costs.

Very low leverage limits interest and refinancing pressure, giving Invivyd greater flexibility to fund clinical programs and commercial operations. This provides a stronger financial base than a highly indebted biotech, although continued losses still threaten capital durability.

Advancing pivotal recruitment, a favorable safety-related monitoring change, and commercial growth strengthen the platform’s path toward broader adoption. Confirmed variant neutralization and an expanding infectious-disease pipeline could reduce dependence on one COVID product over time.

bear.b: Large operating losses and sustained negative cash generation mean the company remains dependent on external financing while clinical spending continues. Unless product revenue scales or costs decline materially, dilution and reduced financial flexibility remain persistent risks.

The end of the EUA creates a durable regulatory dependency: Invivyd must secure a clear approval pathway to preserve authorization and commercial continuity. Delays or unfavorable FDA requirements could constrain access to PEMGARDA and increase development and compliance costs.

Failure to regain compliance by January 19, 2027 could lead to additional remedial steps or delisting. Listing uncertainty can complicate capital raising, reduce institutional accessibility, and add operational distraction while the company is funding costly clinical programs.
